title: Introduction

canonicalEdition.name: First edition
canonicalEdition.sourceProvenance: Frozen web bundle only: bibliographic records, table-of-contents evidence, official publication metadata, and narrow secondary summary support. Paraphrase-first; no full text frozen.

anchorSummary: The introduction establishes the book's central promise: this is not a management playbook for tidy cases but a guide for moments when founders are overwhelmed, isolated, and still responsible for the next move.
coreClaim: The hard thing in leadership is not ambition or planning but staying effective when the company is hurting and no painless option exists.
distinctMechanism: Horowitz reframes the book as an operator's survival manual by contrasting polished business advice with the lonely, sleep-losing reality of running a company in crisis.
requiredAnchors: Opening contrast: management books often skip the truly painful parts of the job.
The struggle frame: CEOs face fear, doubt, and brutal decisions without a formula that removes the burden.
Lived-advice promise: the book will rely on lived startup experience rather than abstract leadership theory.
specificApplications: Recognize that leadership problems often begin where templates stop helping.
Frame crisis management as a repeated judgment burden rather than a one-time trick.
Use the struggle lens to evaluate later advice for practical honesty.
commonMisreadings: Treating the introduction as generic startup inspiration instead of a contract about the kind of hard situations the book will face directly.
Assuming the struggle is only emotional rather than operational, strategic, and managerial at the same time.
hardEdgeRequirement: Hard mode must show why no framework can remove the CEO's responsibility once the company is in danger and every option hurts someone.
thresholdQuestion: What do you do when the advice sounds clean but the real situation gives you only bad choices?
